description: Outbound policy data feed to the data warehouse is failing silently. The ETL pipeline shows as successful but the data warehouse tables are not being updated. Report writers have noticed that claims and policy counts in BI dashboards have been static for 3 days.
resolution_notes: The ETL connector was swallowing a schema mismatch error introduced when a new field was added to the policy export format without updating the data warehouse landing table schema. The connector was configured to skip unrecognized columns silently. Fixed by adding the new column to the data warehouse schema and updating the connector to fail loudly on schema mismatches. Data warehouse tables are now current after a backfill run.

description: Users across all teams are being logged out every 30-45 minutes regardless of activity. The issue started this morning and is affecting all three centers -- PolicyCenter, ClaimCenter and BillingCenter. Users have to log back in multiple times per hour which is severely disrupting work.
resolution_notes: The session timeout value in the application server config had been accidentally set to 30 minutes during routine maintenance last night (the intended value was 480 minutes / 8 hours). Reverted the session timeout to 480 minutes and restarted the app server. Confirmed sessions are now persisting correctly.

description: ClaimCenter search is extremely slow during peak hours (10am-2pm). Searching by claimant name or policy number takes 25-40 seconds to return results. Off-peak searches complete in under 2 seconds. The issue has been present for about a week and is getting worse as claim volume grows.
resolution_notes: Database query analysis showed that the full-text index on the claim search table had become severely fragmented after a bulk data import last week. Rebuilt the index during a maintenance window and query times immediately dropped back to under 1 second. Scheduled weekly index maintenance to prevent recurrence.

description: Customer called in saying their autopay failed for the 3rd month in a row even though their card on file is valid and has sufficient funds. No error is shown to the customer in the portal -- the payment just silently doesn't happen.
resolution_notes: turned out the card's expiry month/year got swapped during a data migration (MM/YY stored as YY/MM for this one customer's record). payment gateway rejected it every time bc the expiry looked like it was in the past. corrected the two fields directly in billingcenter admin screen. customer confirmed autopay worked on next cycle.

description: Scheduled overnight batch job for invoice generation is producing duplicate invoices for commercial accounts with multi-vehicle policies. Customers are receiving two copies of the same invoice by email. Finance team has flagged approximately 200 duplicate invoices since last Monday.
resolution_notes: The invoice generation batch was accidentally registered twice in the job scheduler after a config file was edited during a manual hotfix. Removed the duplicate job entry from the quartz scheduler config, cleared the duplicate invoice records from the database, and sent corrected invoices to affected customers. Added a startup validation check to detect duplicate job registrations.

summary: Refund calculation rounding error under review
description: Billing team flagged refund amounts off by a few cents on prorated cancellations. A fix changing the rounding mode to banker's rounding has been coded and is pending QA sign-off.
resolution_notes: Changed rounding strategy from HALF_UP to HALF_EVEN in the refund calculator. Fix is in review, not yet merged to the release branch.

summary: Invoice generation job silently skipping accounts with autopay
description: Monthly invoice batch completed with 0 errors reported, but ~1,200 autopay accounts received no invoice. Discovered by finance reconciliation, not by monitoring.
resolution_notes: The autopay filter condition in InvoiceGenBatch.gs used an outdated boolean field (cg_autopayenabled_legacy) instead of the new cg_autopayenrollment entity introduced in BillingCenter 2025.1. Config change to point filter at the new entity. Recommending a monitoring alert on invoice-count-vs-active-accounts going forward.

summary: ClaimCenter UI extremely slow during peak hours
description: Adjusters report 10-15 second page loads on the claim summary screen between 12pm-2pm daily for the past week.
resolution_notes: APM traces showed N+1 query pattern in the new ClaimActivitySummary widget fetching related activities one-by-one instead of batching. Code fix to use a single batched query. Page load dropped to under 1.5s under load test.

summary: Claim status sync failing to external adjuster portal
description: Claim status updates made in ClaimCenter aren't propagating to the external third-party adjuster portal. Adjusters are working off stale claim statuses, causing confusion on active claims.
resolution_notes: The outbound webhook was silently failing on claims with a null sub-status field, which the portal's new schema required as non-null. Added a default sub-status fallback before the webhook payload is built. Backfilled stale statuses for the affected 120 claims.

description: Claim reserve amounts on the adjuster dashboard are displaying in the wrong currency for international claims. USD amounts are being displayed as GBP for claims filed in the UK region. The correct currency is stored in the database but the display layer is showing the wrong symbol. Adjusters can see the correct value by running a manual report.
resolution_notes: The dashboard widget for claim reserves was using a hardcoded currency formatter that defaulted to GBP for any claim with a UK office code. Updated the formatter to read the currency code from the claim record itself instead of inferring it from office code. No data was incorrect -- only the display label was wrong.

summary: Claim document upload timing out for large PDFs
description: Adjusters report claim document uploads timing out for PDF files over 15MB. Fix has been identified and deployed to staging, currently being validated before production rollout.
resolution_notes: Increased upload timeout threshold and added chunked upload support. Currently under validation in staging -- not yet promoted to production.

description: Shared contact records for agents who are licensed in multiple states are showing duplicate address entries after a recent data migration. PolicyCenter policy screens and ClaimCenter claim screens both display the duplicate addresses, causing confusion for staff. No data is lost but the duplication is visually confusing and may cause downstream address selection errors.
resolution_notes: The data migration script for the multi-state agent contact records ran the address import twice due to a missing idempotency check. Identified and removed the duplicate address records from ContactManager. Added an idempotency check to the migration script to prevent re-importing records that already exist. Verified PolicyCenter and ClaimCenter both show clean single-address contact records for all affected agents.

summary: Duplicate contact records created after account merge
description: Running the account merge utility on linked policyholder records is creating duplicate contact entries instead of merging them, causing inconsistent address/phone data across PolicyCenter and BillingCenter.
resolution_notes: Found the merge utility was comparing contact IDs instead of a normalized name+DOB+SSN hash. Updated the matching key and re-ran the merge for the affected 60 contacts. Verified no remaining duplicates.

summary: Portal login SSO fix awaiting change advisory board sign-off
description: Agents using SSO to log into the Digital Portal are intermittently getting logged out mid-session, forcing re-authentication. A fix adjusting the SSO token refresh interval has been developed and is pending CAB sign-off before deployment.
resolution_notes: SSO token refresh was set to a shorter interval than the identity provider's token lifetime, causing premature expiry. Adjusted refresh interval to align with IdP token lifetime. Fix is pending change advisory board approval, not yet deployed.

description: All inbound FNOL notifications from the mobile app are being dropped. Claims are not being created in ClaimCenter from mobile submissions. The mobile app shows a success confirmation to customers but no claim appears in the system. Approximately 90 mobile FNOLs have been silently lost since yesterday evening.
resolution_notes: An SSL certificate on the inbound FNOL API endpoint expired at midnight. The mobile app received a successful handshake response from the load balancer before the certificate check, but the payload was dropped by the API gateway when it attempted to forward to ClaimCenter. Renewed the certificate, restarted the API gateway, and manually recreated the 90 lost FNOL records from the mobile app's submission logs.

description: The nightly sync job that pushes updated policy data to the agency management system partner started failing silently two nights ago -- no alert fired.
resolution_notes: the job's failure alert was wired to a monitoring channel that had been archived during an unrelated cleanup last month, so failures went unnoticed. fixed the actual sync issue (an expired API key) and rewired the alert to the correct active monitoring channel. verified both the sync and the alert now work.

description: Agents could not bind new commercial property policies -- the bind button threw a generic error with no detail, blocking all new business for that line.
resolution_notes: found a missing required field mapping for a new state-specific disclosure form added last week. added the missing mapping to the bind workflow. verified binds succeed in all affected states now.

description: Executive dashboard showing written premium by line of business is displaying figures from the previous quarter instead of the current quarter. Report writers flagged that the ETL job that feeds the dashboard stopped updating three days ago. Underwriters are pulling manual reports as a workaround.
resolution_notes: The ETL job that feeds the written premium dashboard had a date filter hardcoded to the previous quarter, introduced when the job was cloned from a quarterly snapshot task. Updated the date filter to use a rolling current-quarter calculation. Reran the ETL job and confirmed the dashboard now shows current figures.

description: Agents report that the renewal quote screen freezes for about 15 seconds every time they click 'Calculate Premium' on auto policies with more than 3 vehicles. Screen eventually loads but agents think the system has crashed and often click the button multiple times, creating duplicate rating calls.
resolution_notes: root cause -- rating engine was looping thru each vehicle sequentially instead of batching the call. fixed by batching vehicle rating requests into a single call. tested w/ 5-vehicle policy, load time dropped from 15s to under 2s. pushed to prod 12/10 9am.

description: Underwriting rules engine is returning incorrect premium calculations for home policies with a swimming pool endorsement. Agents can manually override the calculated premium as a temporary workaround. The issue affects roughly 30% of new home policy quotes in the last two weeks.
resolution_notes: Traced to a Gosu rule that was using an outdated endorsement factor table reference. The old table was deprecated in the last release but the reference was never updated. Updated the Gosu rule to point to the correct table, ran regression tests, and redeployed. No data cleanup needed as manually overridden premiums were already correct.

summary: Policy submission stuck in 'Processing' after 2025.2 upgrade
description: Underwriters report new business submissions in PolicyCenter hang indefinitely in Processing state. Started immediately after the 2025.2.1 upgrade was deployed to production last night. No error visible to end users, but app server logs show repeated GosuRuntimeException in PolicyPeriod.bind().
resolution_notes: Root cause was a Gosu rule override (UWApprovalRule.gs) referencing a deprecated API method removed in 2025.2.1 (PolicyPeriod.getLatestPeriod() renamed to getLatestBoundPeriod()). Patched the custom rule, redeployed, cleared stuck submissions via batch script. Confirmed with Guidewire release notes GW-RN-2025-2-1-004 which documented this breaking change.

description: A single underwriter reported that one specific rate table lookup returns a rate that is slightly higher than expected for a niche vehicle class in one state. All other rate lookups are unaffected. The discrepancy is small (a few dollars) and does not block quoting.
resolution_notes: Investigation found the rate table had a correctly configured value -- it simply reflected a rate change that had been approved by the state regulator two weeks prior and had not yet been communicated to the underwriting team. No defect existed; the rate was correct as configured. Ticket closed as user error / expectation mismatch, and underwriting was notified of the regulator-approved rate change.
